image.description: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

item.title: US midterm election results: Democrats flip House and Senate. Here's what else the data tells us
item.description: Democrats have won the majority in both House and Senate. Vote counts are still ongoing. DW takes a look at who voted Republican, who voted Democrat and what it all means.
item.dc:subject: TOP STORIES

item.title: US midterms: Democrats gain control of House and Senate from Republicans
item.description: The Democratic Party gained control of the House and Senate, delivering a stinging rebuke to US President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. Follow DW's live updates.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: India news: Election body opens door for voter reinclusion
item.description: The Indian poll body said no action will be taken against deleted voters for using Form 6 for re-enrolment in voter rolls. Follow DW for more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
item.description: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: US to cut nearly $4 billion in Israel military aid, Trump says
item.description: President Donald Trump said that the United States would still sell weapons to Israel. He added that Democratic candidates were using US military support for Israel against Republicans in the midterm elections.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Spain transport minister offers resignation in wake of train accident
item.description: After two deadly train crashes this year, Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente has said he will step down.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Greenland's parliament ratifies Trump's US security agreement
item.description: The US is set to expand its military footprint on the Arctic island, part of the Kingdom of Denmark. It follows pressure from Donald Trump earlier in the year which opened a major rift in the transatlantic alliance.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: UK's King Charles III decries 'monstrous injustice' of slave trade
item.description: King Charles has told leaders at a Commonwealth summit that the legacy of the transatlantic slave trade "fills my heart with horror." He did not address calls for apologies and reparations.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Why South Africa's local elections matter
item.description: South Africans head to the polls on Wednesday amid water shortages, frustration with local services and questions over whether the ANC's support will keep falling.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ukraine war: Merz doubts Russia is serious about a truce
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met with Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Berlin. Both leaders said the EU needs to be included in peace talks with Russia. Merz also expressed doubts that Russia is serious about seeking a truce.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: China and India achieved diplomatic thaw. Now the border is flaring up
item.description: Indian authorities have confirmed a new border "face-off" between Indian and Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh, raising questions about the still fragile thaw in relations between New Delhi and Beijing.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
item.description: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
item.description: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: What US midterm elections mean for Ukraine, Iran and elsewhere
item.description: Donald Trump's Republicans control the US Congress, but that could change after the midterm elections. The outcome of the ballot will not only impact domestic policy but also conflicts in Europe and the Middle East.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
item.description: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Yemen: Houthi clashes near Taiz leave residents in a 'state of panic'
item.description: Fighting between Iran-backed Houthi rebels and Yemeni government forces has intensified around the city of Taiz. Residents face growing shortages of food, water and medical supplies as thousands flee their homes.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can US midterm election really change Trump's Iran policy?
item.description: The US midterms are at hand, but their impact on the Iran war remains far from clear. Analysts say the Washington political elite may not be as divided on Iran as it appears.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
item.description: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
item.description: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
item.description: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany news: Ukraine in focus at Berlin Security Conference
item.description: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
item.description: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
item.description: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
item.description: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
item.description: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
item.description: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's second term is due to end in March next year. Meanwhile, Merz has called for 'digital sovereignty' in the era of AI.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
item.description: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
item.description: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
item.description: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany's search for a nuclear waste site
item.description: Finland has become the first country with a final storage facility for nuclear waste. Germany is still searching for a site, while some countries have yet to start. Costs are expected to total many billions of euros.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
item.description: After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany's Gen Z protests disrupted by violence on Saturday
item.description: Nationwide protests led by young people were largely peaceful throughout the day, but reports about looting and rioting in the evening, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the spirit of the demonstrations.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
item.description: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
item.description: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
item.description: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
item.description: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Many Turkish 'guest workers' hit by poverty in old age
item.description: West Germany and Turkey signed an agreement allowing the temporary recruitment of workers on October 30, 1961. Sixty-five years on, many so-called 'guest workers' can't live from their pensions.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
item.description: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
item.description: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
item.description: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
item.description: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany seeks new head of state
item.description: The question of who should become Germany's new presiden is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
item.description: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
item.description: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
item.description: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
item.description: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
item.description: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
item.description: Young people in Germany are preparing to protest over education and climate change. Politicians fear violence like in France, but an expert sees differences.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
item.description: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
item.description: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
item.description: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
item.description: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
item.description: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
item.description: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
item.description: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
item.description: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
item.description: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
item.description: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
item.description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
item.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
item.description: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
item.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
item.description: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
item.description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
item.description: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
item.description: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return
item.description: Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
item.description: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
item.description: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
item.description: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany news: AfD's Weidel calls for major EU reforms
item.description: Far-right Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel reveals the party's plan to reform the EU. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in Berlin to talk to developers and investors. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
item.description: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
item.description: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
item.description: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
item.description: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
item.description: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
item.description: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
item.description: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
item.description: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
item.description: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
item.description: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
item.description: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
item.description: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
item.description: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
item.description: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
item.description: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
item.description: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
item.description: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's PM in a political tangle
item.description: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
item.description: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
item.description: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for better structures globally.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
item.description: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
item.description: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
item.description: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
item.description: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
item.description: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
item.description: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check
item.description: Greener buses and cleaner fleets are reshaping public transport across Europe. But are cities moving fast enough to meet their zero-emission goals?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
item.description: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
item.description: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
item.description: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
item.description: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
item.description: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
item.description: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: 2026 Nobel Prize winner Anne Carson: Where to start reading
item.description: The works of this year's Nobel Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.

item.title: Early-onset cancer rising worldwide: Causes, risk, prevention
item.description: Across Latin America, early-onset cancer rates have risen, especially of bowel, breast and cervical cancers. But it is a worldwide trend.

item.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
item.description: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

item.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
item.description: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: '90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
item.description: The 1990s are remembered for Brit-pop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Nobel Prize in chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
item.description: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
item.description: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ronaldo stays on under cloud as Messi exits internationals
item.description: Just hours before Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo posted his latest salvo in a row with Portugal. Ronaldo wants to play on despite the troubles, while Messi bathed in adulation.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
item.description: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US
item.description: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. While the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the world's poorest countries are banking on solar, wind and water instead.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics
item.description: The International Olympic Committee has revealed the six other countries intending to bid for the 2036 Olympic Games. This comes after Germany selected Munich as its Olympic candidate.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
item.description: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival efforts from Netflix.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Nobel Prize in literature: How the winner is secretly chosen
item.description: Can Xue is considered one of this year's favorites; Margaret Atwood and Salman Rushdie are other strong contenders. But what goes on behind the scenes in the selection of the Nobel Prize in literature?
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: AI models keep hacking real systems during tests. What does this mean?
item.description: AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.
